note: Teaching plan for Classroom mode. Each lesson carries a vetted romanized lexicon per language (kn/hi/ta); the teacher LLM must use exactly these forms and never native script. Forms are colloquial spoken (Bangalore Kannada, Delhi Hindi, Chennai Tamil). Lexicon entries are 'english = romanized form'; lines starting with 'note:' are teaching notes. No em dashes anywhere.

lessons.title: Greetings and courtesies
lessons.objective: Greet someone, ask how they are, and say please, thank you, sorry, yes and no.
teach: a natural hello and a reply
lessons.grammar: These are fixed everyday phrases, no grammar yet. Focus on natural pronunciation.
practice: Have the student greet you and ask how you are
Have them thank you for something

kn: hello = namaskara (the reply is also namaskara)
note: in daily life people very often just say the English word thanks; teach dhanyavadagalu but mention this
note: for sorry too, most people simply say the English word sorry
hi: hello = namaste (the reply is also namaste)
how are you = aap kaise hain
note: to a woman it is aap kaisi hain; mention this briefly
I am fine = main theek hoon
thank you = dhanyavaad (shukriya is also very common)
please = kripya
sorry = maaf kijiye
yes = haan
no = nahin
ta: hello = vanakkam (the reply is also vanakkam)
please = konjam (literally a little, used to soften requests; Tamils rarely say a separate word for please)
note: in daily life most people just say the English word sorry

lessons.title: About yourself
lessons.objective: Say your name, where you are from, and ask someone their name.
lessons.grammar: Introduce the idea of 'my' and 'your'. Keep it to fixed patterns for now.
practice: Have the student introduce themselves fully
Have them ask you your name and where you are from

kn: what is your name = nimma hesaru enu
I am from ___ (my home town is ___) = nanna ooru ___
nice to meet you = nimmannu bheti aagi santosha
hi: my name is ___ = mera naam ___ hai
what is your name = aapka naam kya hai
I am from ___ = main ___ se hoon
nice to meet you = aapse milkar khushi hui
ta: what is your name = unga peru enna
I am from ___ (my home town is ___) = en ooru ___
nice to meet you = ungala paathadhula sandhosham

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 20
lessons.objective: Count from 1 to 20 and ask how many.
lessons.grammar: Just vocabulary and counting. Drill the numbers in groups of five, and recall each group before starting the next.
practice: Have the student count 1 to 10
Ask how many fingers you are holding up and have them answer

kn: one to five = ondu, eradu, mooru, naalku, aidu
six to ten = aaru, elu, entu, ombattu, hattu
eleven to fifteen = hannondu, hanneradu, hadimooru, hadinaalku, hadinaidu
sixteen to twenty = hadinaaru, hadinelu, hadinentu, hattombattu, ippattu
hi: one to five = ek, do, teen, chaar, paanch
six to ten = chhe, saat, aath, nau, das
eleven to fifteen = gyaarah, baarah, terah, chaudah, pandrah
sixteen to twenty = solah, satrah, athaarah, unnees, bees
how many = kitne
ta: one to five = onnu, rendu, moonu, naalu, anju
six to ten = aaru, ezhu, ettu, onbadhu, patthu
eleven to fifteen = padhinonnu, pannendu, padhimoonu, padhinaalu, padhinanju
sixteen to twenty = padhinaaru, padhinezhu, padhinettu, patthonbadhu, irubadhu

lessons.title: Fruits
lessons.objective: Name common fruits and say 'this is a ...'.
lessons.grammar: Introduce 'this is' plus a noun. One simple pattern. In these languages there is no word for 'is' needed: 'this' plus the noun is a full sentence.
practice: Point to imaginary fruits and have the student name them
Have them say 'this is a mango' with two other fruits

kn: apple = sebu (most people just say apple)
orange = kittale (most people just say orange)
this is ___ = idu ___ (idu maavina hannu = this is a mango)
hi: banana = kela
mango = aam
apple = seb
orange = santra
grapes = angoor
this is ___ = yeh ___ hai (yeh aam hai = this is a mango)
ta: apple = apple (Tamils use the English word)
orange = orange (Tamils use the English word)
this is ___ = idhu ___ (idhu maampazham = this is a mango)

lessons.title: Food and drink
lessons.objective: Name everyday food and drink staples.
lessons.grammar: More nouns, reuse 'this is' and introduce 'I want' informally.
practice: Have the student order a tea and a rice
Have them name three foods

kn: tea = tea (everyone says the English word; chai is also heard)
tomato = tomato (everyone says the English word)
I want ___ = nanage ___ beku (nanage tea beku = I want tea)
hi: rice = chaawal
water = paani
milk = doodh
tea = chai
onion = pyaaz
tomato = tamaatar
I want ___ = mujhe ___ chaahiye (mujhe chai chaahiye = I want tea)
ta: tea = tea (everyone says the English word)
I want ___ = enakku ___ venum (enakku tea venum = I want tea)

lessons.title: Family
lessons.grammar: Note that these languages distinguish elder and younger siblings. Point this out gently with one example.
practice: Have the student describe their own family in a few short sentences

hi: mother = maa
father = papa (pitaji is more formal)
elder brother = bada bhai (elder sister = badi behen)
younger sister = chhoti behen (younger brother = chhota bhai)
child = bachcha
my mother = meri maa

lessons.title: Everyday things
lessons.grammar: Reuse 'this is' and introduce 'where is'. Build toward asking for things.
practice: Have the student name three objects near them
Have them ask where the phone is

kn: phone = phone (everyone says the English word)
where is ___ = ___ elli ide (phone elli ide = where is the phone)
hi: house = ghar
door = darwaaza
phone = phone (everyone says the English word)
money = paisa
chair = kursi
book = kitaab
where is ___ = ___ kahaan hai (phone kahaan hai = where is the phone)
ta: phone = phone (everyone says the English word)
where is ___ = ___ enga irukku (phone enga irukku = where is the phone)

lessons.title: This and that
lessons.objective: Say this is X, that is Y, and ask is this X.
lessons.grammar: Demonstratives. There is no separate word for 'is': 'this' plus a noun is a full sentence. The yes/no question is made with a small ending sound, not a new word.
practice: Have the student ask you three 'is this?' questions and answer them

kn: this is ___ = idu ___ (idu neeru = this is water)
that is ___ = adu ___ (adu maavina hannu = that is a mango)
is this ___? = idu ___ aa? (idu haalaa? = is this milk? just add the aa sound to the noun)
hi: this = yeh
that = voh
this is ___ = yeh ___ hai (yeh paani hai = this is water)
that is ___ = voh ___ hai (voh aam hai = that is a mango)
is this ___? = kya yeh ___ hai? (kya yeh doodh hai? = is this milk?)
ta: this is ___ = idhu ___ (idhu thanni = this is water)
that is ___ = adhu ___ (adhu maampazham = that is a mango)
is this ___? = idhu ___ aa? (idhu paalaa? = is this milk? just add the aa sound to the noun)

lessons.title: I want, I have, I need
lessons.objective: Express wanting, having and needing something.
lessons.grammar: These are fixed frames: learn the frame, drop any noun in. Point out that want and need share one word in Kannada and Tamil.
practice: Have the student say three things they want
Have them say one thing they do not want

kn: I do not want ___ = nanage ___ beda
I have ___ = nanna hatra ___ ide (nanna hatra duddu ide = I have money)
I need ___ = nanage ___ beku (same word as want; Kannada does not separate them)
hi: I want ___ = mujhe ___ chaahiye
I do not want ___ = mujhe ___ nahin chaahiye
I have ___ = mere paas ___ hai (mere paas paisa hai = I have money)
I need ___ = mujhe ___ ki zaroorat hai
ta: I do not want ___ = enakku ___ vendam
I have ___ = en kitta ___ irukku (en kitta kaasu irukku = I have money)
I need ___ = enakku ___ venum (same word as want; Tamil does not separate them)

lessons.title: Asking questions
lessons.objective: Ask what, where, how much, how many, and who.
lessons.grammar: Question words. Show where the question word sits by reusing sentences they already know.
practice: Have the student haggle: ask how much, say it is too much
Have them ask where three things are

kn: how much = eshtu (idu eshtu? = how much is this?)
how many = eshtu (same word as how much)
hi: what is this = yeh kya hai
where is ___ = ___ kahaan hai
how much = kitna (yeh kitne ka hai? = how much is this?)
how many = kitne
who = kaun
ta: how much = evvalavu (idhu evvalavu? = how much is this?)

lessons.title: Present tense
lessons.objective: Say what you do: I eat, I drink, I go, I speak, I come.
lessons.grammar: The present tense 'I' form. Point out that the verb comes at the END of the sentence: I rice eat, not I eat rice.
practice: Have the student say three things they do every day

kn: I eat = naanu tintini (naanu anna tintini = I eat rice)
I go = naanu hogtini (naanu manege hogtini = I go home)
I speak = naanu maatadtini (naanu swalpa Kannada maatadtini = I speak a little Kannada)
hi: I eat = main khaata hoon (main chaawal khaata hoon = I eat rice)
I drink = main peeta hoon
I go = main jaata hoon (main ghar jaata hoon = I go home)
I speak = main bolta hoon (main thodi Hindi bolta hoon = I speak a little Hindi)
I come = main aata hoon
note: these are the forms a man uses; a woman says khaati, peeti, jaati, bolti, aati. Teach the form matching the student and mention the other once
ta: I eat = naan saapdren (naan saadham saapdren = I eat rice)
I go = naan poren (naan veetukku poren = I go home)
I speak = naan pesuren (naan konjam Tamil pesuren = I speak a little Tamil)

lessons.title: Past tense
lessons.objective: Say what you did: I ate, I went, I came, I saw.
lessons.grammar: The past tense 'I' form. Contrast one verb in present and past so the ending change is heard clearly.
practice: Have the student tell you three things they did today

kn: I ate = naanu tinde (naanu anna tinde = I ate rice)
I went = naanu hode (naanu manege hode = I went home)
note: contrast pair to teach the ending: tintini (I eat) vs tinde (I ate)
hi: I ate = maine khaaya (maine chaawal khaaya = I ate rice)
I went = main gaya (a woman says main gayi)
I came = main aaya (a woman says main aayi)
I saw = maine dekha
note: teach khaaya and dekha as fixed phrases with maine; do not explain the maine grammar, it comes later
ta: I ate = naan saapten (naan saadham saapten = I ate rice)
I went = naan ponen (naan veetukku ponen = I went home)
note: contrast pair to teach the ending: saapdren (I eat) vs saapten (I ate)

lessons.title: Future tense
lessons.objective: Say what you will do: I will eat, I will go, I will come.
lessons.grammar: The future 'I' form. Now the student has all three tenses of one verb.
practice: Have the student say one thing they will do tomorrow
Have them say one verb in past, present and future

kn: note: spoken Kannada uses the PRESENT form for the future, with a time word doing the work. This is the whole lesson: no new endings
I will eat = naanu tintini (naale tintini = I will eat tomorrow)
I will go = naanu hogtini (naale hogtini = I will go tomorrow)
hi: tomorrow = kal
I will eat = main khaaunga (a woman says khaaungi)
I will go = main jaaunga (jaaungi) (main kal jaaunga = I will go tomorrow)
I will come = main aaunga (aaungi)
I will speak = main bolunga (bolungi)
ta: I will go = naan poven (naan naalaikku poven = I will go tomorrow)

lessons.title: Building sentences
lessons.objective: Join words into longer sentences and use and, but, because.
lessons.grammar: Reinforce that the verb goes last, and show how to join two ideas.
examples_en: I will go home because it is late.
practice: Have the student join two short sentences with and
Have them give a reason using because

kn: and = mattu (tea mattu anna = tea and rice)
note: word order is subject, object, verb: naanu anna tintini = I rice eat
hi: and = aur (chai aur chaawal = tea and rice)
but = lekin
because = kyunki
note: word order is subject, object, verb: main chaawal khaata hoon = I rice eat
ta: and = add um to both words (tea-um saadham-um = tea and rice)
note: word order is subject, object, verb: naan saadham saapdren = I rice eat

lessons.title: Being polite and saying no
lessons.objective: Make polite requests and say there isn't or I don't want.
lessons.grammar: Polite request forms and negation. This ties the whole course together.
practice: Have the student make three polite requests
Have the student hold a 30 second chat with you using everything they know

kn: please give = kodi (swalpa neeru kodi = please give a little water)
can you say it again = innomme heli (say it once more)
there is no ___ = ___ illa (haalu illa = there is no milk)
I do not want = nanage beda
hi: a little = thoda
please give = dijiye (thoda paani dijiye = please give a little water)
can you say it again = phir se boliye
there is no ___ = ___ nahin hai (doodh nahin hai = there is no milk)
I do not want = mujhe nahin chaahiye
ta: please give = kudunga (konjam thanni kudunga = please give a little water)
can you say it again = thirumba sollunga
there is no ___ = ___ illa (paal illa = there is no milk)
I do not want = enakku vendam
